persons.name: Amy
persons.harm: Catfished on Plenty of Fish in 2016 by a man posing as 'Eric'; when she refused odd photo requests he posted her intimate photos with her name and home address, then cyberstalked her for about five years: emails, calls, voicemails, fake profiles with her nude photos, impersonating her on crime victims' pages, attacking her company, employees, colleagues and family.
persons.perpetrator_role: a stranger she met on a dating site (catfish), later identified as a man in New Jersey

quotes.quote: I don't recall telling anybody about it, but I was so terrified I deleted the email and printed it because I didn't even feel comfortable forwarding it to my personal email address.

contacts.when: 2016, the night the photos were posted
contacts.what_was_asked: Help identifying and stopping the man who posted her photos and threatened her.
contacts.what_institution_did: An officer came, listened, gave her a card, and said nothing could be done without a name and location.
contacts.quote: given I had no idea who this person actually was or where they were located for that matter, they couldn't do anything. I just remember them giving me a card and they're like, if you get any more information to help us identify who they are, then let us know. We want to help you. But until then, there's not much we can do.
contacts.what_happened_next: No investigation; she reported to the site herself and tried to move on.
contacts.notes: She says the officer was kind; the code reflects no concrete step, not disbelief.

contacts.what_institution_did: Nothing came of repeated reports.
contacts.quote: I did report his profiles to plenty of fish multiple times, nothing came of it, which is extremely frustrating.
contacts.what_happened_next: She deleted the site; contact resumed by email in January 2017.

contacts.what_was_asked: Federal help identifying and stopping the stalker.
contacts.what_institution_did: No response to any of four reports.
contacts.quote: the fourth report to the FBI was May of 2020 and at that point I just kind of gave up.
contacts.what_happened_next: Daily harassment continued through 2020; 'I had submitted multiple reports to the FBI at this point ... and I hadn't heard anything.'
contacts.notes: Four reports to the same institution with the same (non-)response are recorded as one contact.

contacts.institution: social media platforms (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok)
contacts.what_was_asked: Take down fake profiles using her name and nude photos.
contacts.what_institution_did: Reports by Amy, family, colleagues and her PR firm did not get the accounts removed; some remain up.
contacts.quote: There should be some accountability for some of these social media platforms where there were false profiles of my daughter created. We knew it. She reported it. They just seemed unwilling to cooperate with doing the right thing and trying to get those shut down.
contacts.what_happened_next: Fake accounts still online at the update episode; she found pursuing takedowns 'too overwhelming'.
contacts.notes: Her mother: 'those platforms are still up and running on social media And social media refuses to take them down.' (s19-e3 @ 22:37). Initiated by Amy herself as well as friends/family.

contacts.institution: FBI Denver field office (special agent on duty)
contacts.what_was_asked: Advice on what to do about the online stalking.
contacts.what_institution_did: The agent listened and escalated to the cyber crime unit; a case was opened through Denver Police in January 2021.
contacts.quote: I actually got a special agent on duty. I don't know what I said to him, but he listened to me and heard me and heard my story and escalated my case to the cyber crime unit within the FBI field office here. As a result, a case was officially opened actually through the Denver Police Department in January of 2021.
contacts.what_happened_next: A Denver detective on the FBI cybercrime task force took the case.
contacts.notes: Call made after her business partner pushed for action and attorneys were consulted.

contacts.institution: FBI victim advocate's office (later DA/state victim advocates)
contacts.what_institution_did: Called her, offered resources including money for therapy and an assigned advocate; later reimbursed therapy and guided her through hearings.
contacts.quote: she just basically told me that there's a bunch of resources available. Everything from money for therapy, money for rehab, as well as tools and resources and an individual who'll be assigned to my case to guide me through the process.
contacts.what_happened_next: 'I was reimbursed for therapy sessions that I had.' (s19-e5 @ 50:27)
contacts.notes: Victim notification was slower than her father's own tracking (s19-e4 @ 24:52).

contacts.what_institution_did: Declined to take the case; it stayed a local Denver case.
contacts.quote: Once the case goes into the FBI, the US Attorney's office actually gets involved, and they review the data that's been provided thus far, the documentation, and they decide if they take the case or not. And in this instance, they didn't take it.
contacts.what_happened_next: Investigated and prosecuted locally (Denver).
contacts.notes: Declining did not stop the case; coded as no step by this institution.

contacts.institution: Denver Police Department detective (FBI cybercrime task force) and other agencies
contacts.what_institution_did: Investigated daily, obtained cell tower data and search warrants, identified him in July 2021, searched his New Jersey home in September, arrested him in November 2021 on felony stalking.
contacts.quote: He was arrested in New Jersey and when he was arrested in November of 21, he was charged with a class five felony, which was stalking.
contacts.what_happened_next: Extradited to Denver, held on $50,000 bond, never bonded out.
contacts.notes: During the September search the agent showed him the warrant with Amy's name: 'He should never have known who did that.' (s19-e4 @ 11:22) - this exposure is why harmed_by_institution_ever is true. No arrest at the search; she was left exposed Sept-Nov.

contacts.institution: court clerk, civil protection order filing (Denver)
contacts.what_was_asked: Civil protection order until his arrest.
contacts.what_institution_did: The clerk questioned whether she was in imminent danger; her mother says she was shamed.
contacts.quote: The clerk was standing there flipping through my pages, not sitting down, just kind of leaning over the table and she looked at me and said, you know, you have to be in imminent danger, right? I looked at her and I said, I don't know that I'm not.
contacts.what_happened_next: Outcome of that civil filing not stated; she later obtained a permanent protection order through the criminal case.
contacts.notes: Mother: 'The first time she went to get a restraining order, they were derogatory towards her. They tried to shame her' (s19-e4 @ 15:30).

contacts.what_institution_did: Prosecuted the felony but pressed her early to consider a plea that could reduce it to a misdemeanor.
contacts.quote: this guy doesn't have any prior crimes. The way this typically works is it could be pushed to a misdemeanor, because he had no prior record based on what's in the system currently.
contacts.what_happened_next: She refused; the defendant unexpectedly pleaded guilty to everything.
contacts.notes: She praises the prosecutor; acted_partly reflects the plea pressure. Could also be read as believed_and_acted.

contacts.what_institution_did: Imposed the maximum Colorado sentence (four years plus two years parole) and told Amy it was not her fault; permanent protection order in place.
contacts.quote: He was ultimately sentenced to the maximum sentence that the state of Colorado allows, which is he got four years with time served plus two years of parole. The judge went out of her way to say that there was no sentence that would do Amy Justice, but that she would do what she could.
contacts.what_happened_next: Imprisoned; 'Because I had a criminal case, I do have a permanent protection order against [perpetrator]' (s19-e5 @ 51:32).

contacts.what_institution_did: Chair denied parole herself and made the hearing audio a permanent part of his file.
contacts.quote: I don't typically do this or say this, but I feel like it's necessary to tell you that I am absolutely denying his parole today. And two, I am so sorry for what happened to you.
contacts.what_happened_next: Second hearing May 2024: he was not released early and will leave at his mandatory release date (late 2024 expected).
contacts.notes: Family could not attend; impact statements were only considered after Amy fought for it (s19-e5 @ 31:40). Parole hearing audio was played on air.

persons.outcome_quote: What I want you to hear is that I know the defendant is capable of so much worse than the crime he's being sentenced for today. It's for that reason, the only time I've ever felt safe in over five years is when he's in jail.
persons.decisive_work_quote: Amy gave them so much information. She documented everything. There was a huge electronic file. She had snippets of voice messages that were left, text messages,
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: about four and a half years after her first police report in 2016; nine months after her first IC3 report (case opened January 2021)
persons.notes: Outcome coded protected because arrest and incarceration stopped the active stalking and she says she feels safe only while he is jailed; but fake accounts remain online ('she is still being victimized because of the technology', father, s19-e5 @ 42:06) and his release (late 2024) loomed at the last update, so partly_protected is defensible. Decisive work: she pressed repeatedly after police/IC3/platform inaction and documented everything; the detective's own investigation (cell tower data, warrants) was also essential. The 2017 email went unreported. Perpetrator named on air; replaced with [perpetrator].

contacts.what_institution_did: Security did a sweep, then told her it was housekeeping checking the room; their attitude changed once it was a staff member, and they did not call police.
contacts.quote: they call me back and they're like, uh, so the person who tried to get into your room works in housekeeping and he was just checking to see if anybody was still staying in the room. But the complete energy had changed as soon as they knew it was a staff member of the hotel.
contacts.what_happened_next: She assumed security had called police; they had not.
contacts.notes: Could also be disbelieved/did_nothing; quote shows closing ranks around staff.

contacts.what_institution_did: Officer tried to rush her off and wrongly said she could not report from out of state; after she asked for his badge number they took a report; nothing came of it.
contacts.quote: I could definitely tell right away the officer could not be less interested in taking a report and was trying to just rush me off the phone. Then he told me I couldn't make a report because I was no longer in the state.
contacts.what_happened_next: 'And they took the report and I do have a case number, but nothing that I know of came of it.'

persons.outcome_quote: And they took the report and I do have a case number, but nothing that I know of came of it.
persons.notes: Host's own incident, which she calls 'pretty minor in terms of trauma'. Her season 16 family abuse is only mentioned, not coded.

persons.name: Jennifer (first boyfriend)
persons.harm: In her mid-20s a man from her church group sexually assaulted her repeatedly in his car, pinned and bruised her, raped her twice (including after a dog bite injury), strangled her, threatened to kill her if she became pregnant, forced Plan B on her, and controlled her while she lived in his mother's house.
persons.perpetrator_role: a man from her church group, later her boyfriend

quotes.quote: aggressively sexually assaulting me. I would have never called it that. It wasn't in my purview.
If I call the cops, which now I know that's a fallacy and not true, he's going to be arrested. This is going to crush him. This is going to ruin his life. This is going to ruin his mom.
Also, I felt so shameful and so guilty. I thought I let this happen. This was my fault.

contacts.what_was_asked: Help with what he was doing.
contacts.what_institution_did: Said they knew other women had had similar experiences with him and wished they would come forward; did nothing.
contacts.quote: my own ecclesiastical leader in these instances knew that this person was doing this to women, but there was nothing being done about it.
contacts.what_happened_next: Abuse continued.
contacts.notes: Could also be protected_itself.

contacts.institution: college campus counselor / honor code (religious university)
contacts.what_institution_did: Told her it was okay to end a friendship and that coming forward could get her expelled under the honor code; no safety plan.
contacts.quote: So I was at fault. In all actuality, if I had come forward, there was a chance I could have been expelled. They told me that and in lieu of giving me a safety plan or connecting me to resources
contacts.what_happened_next: He stalked outside her window; she was later raped.
contacts.notes: 'The advice that I was given on campus was it is okay to end a friendship. And that was it.' (@ 21:39)

contacts.when: while living in his mother's house, before leaving
contacts.what_institution_did: Asked why she thought she deserved it, said she faced excommunication; gave him a calling with young men instead of discipline.
contacts.quote: And he goes, why do you think that you deserve this? That was also coupled with him telling me that I would have to go internally,
contacts.what_happened_next: 'they have their own courts ... that I would be facing excommunication, basically reprimanded for my part in this' while 'he needs a calling and he doesn't need to be reprimanded'.
contacts.notes: Also protected_itself (abuser assigned to youth).

contacts.when: about nine months after the rape, after she left
contacts.what_institution_did: Two male officers questioned her role and whether to believe her.
contacts.quote: And the questions I was getting were things like, well, why did you invite him over? Painting this story and they're also questioning the validity of it and your role in it. Talk about victim blaming.
contacts.what_happened_next: Report taken; investigator later arranged a covert call.
contacts.notes: A friend urged her to report and came with her. Also disbelieved.

contacts.when: after she moved back to Utah
contacts.what_institution_did: Named what happened as domestic violence.
contacts.quote: I got a therapist. And I'll never forget when she looked at me and she goes, Jennifer, you were the victim of domestic violence.
contacts.what_happened_next: Began her healing and path into the field.

contacts.what_institution_did: Arranged a covert call; he denied it; investigator could not arrest but visited his house; the report stays on file.
contacts.quote: The investigator, when we hung up, looked at me. He goes, that man knew exactly what to say to cover his ass. I can't arrest him, but I guarantee I'm going to take a trip out to his house, which is exactly what they did.
contacts.what_happened_next: He called her irate; 'if anything were to ever happen in the future, this will be on record and on file for him forever and always.'

persons.outcome_quote: So this man has a long history of abuses and nothing being done about it. I remember feeling like it was such an injustice
persons.notes: Harm ended when she left with her best friend's help, not through an institution. A second church leader offered help but she did not disclose (not coded as a contact). Bruise photos from her 25th birthday exist but are not read/checked on air. Childhood adversity is background only.

persons.name: Jennifer (husband)
persons.harm: Her husband (father of her two sons) verbally abused her, took money, shoved, pushed and hit her, and punched her in the jaw while she held their newborn.

quotes.quote: And I am being abused at home. So now who am I going to tell? Because I felt like the biggest fraud.

contacts.what_institution_did: Police came; a detective followed up; he fled the state before any arrest is described.
contacts.quote: I did notify law enforcement, it was full police but these were the exact same police that I had trained and I am now looking them in the eye in my living room.
contacts.what_happened_next: 'Their dad ended up taking off. He fled from the police. He drained the bank account completely down to nothing.'

contacts.what_institution_did: Supported her and kept her on.
contacts.quote: she goes, Jennifer, there are so many of us who are survivors. We have board members who are survivors. There are many folks who are survivors. We got you.
contacts.what_happened_next: Legal director arranged her restraining order hearing.

contacts.what_institution_did: Restraining order process completed; he was limited to supervised visits.
contacts.quote: I was still navigating the court system, dealing with all of his stuff. He had to have supervised visits, so I'm having to go down and register.
contacts.what_happened_next: She stayed in the field and later became a coalition director.
contacts.notes: Grant of the order is implied ('I had to go through the entire restraining order process') rather than stated.

persons.outcome_quote: He had to have supervised visits, so I'm having to go down and register. And it was just such a mess and it was so overwhelming.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: the night she first called police
persons.notes: Abuse ended when he fled after police were called; restraining order and supervised visits followed. Whether the flight or the institution stopped the harm is not clear; not_protected is defensible.

persons.name: Lenora Claire
persons.harm: From 2011 a stranger with erotomania who saw her on a magazine cover told her he would stalk her, then sent years of graphic rape, kidnap and murder threats, threatened her boss and husband, tried to take her dog, and in 2017 came to LA Comic Con to kidnap her; after release he resumed stalking.

contacts.what_was_asked: Help with a stack of threats from a documented stalker.
contacts.what_institution_did: Told her to dye her hair and get off the internet.
contacts.quote: I went to police seeking help, and I brought this stack of really intense, very heavy threats. And they looked me in the eye and they told me to dye my hair and get off the internet.
contacts.what_happened_next: 'So they just brushed me off.' She lost her galleries and income.
contacts.notes: 'I go as far as to say that they victim blamed and shame me.'

contacts.what_institution_did: Order could be granted but not served while he moved around the country.
contacts.quote: Just because you can get a restraining order granted, if they evade, you have no way to get it to them. And restraining orders don't go into effect until they're served.
contacts.what_happened_next: She tracked his IP herself.

contacts.what_was_asked: Act on death threats to her boss.
contacts.what_institution_did: Nothing.
contacts.quote: So I take his death threats to the police and I'm like, it's not just me. I thought maybe it's it's happening to a man. I still got absolutely nothing from LAPD.
contacts.what_happened_next: She went public in 2015 (Crime Watch Daily, Jezebel).

contacts.institution: police called to another victim's workplace
contacts.what_institution_did: Detained him, served her pending restraining order, released him.
contacts.quote: They didn't arrest him. They detained him and they saw my pending restraining order and they served him and then let him go.
contacts.what_happened_next: First TRO in effect.

contacts.what_was_asked: Help getting law enforcement to act.
contacts.what_institution_did: Brought her to meet the chief of police and the district attorney.
contacts.quote: very rapidly, he took me into meet with the chief of police, the then district attorney and got all that stuff going.
contacts.what_happened_next: No arrest described as a result.
contacts.notes: Introduced by a friend who is also a stalking survivor.

contacts.what_institution_did: Elevated her case after a national TV special and assigned a good detective; but did not work weekends when he announced a kidnap plan.
contacts.quote: My case because of all of that and being on the show was then elevated at LAPD. They have a unit called the threat management unit, which is the best in the entire country.
contacts.what_happened_next: 'I'm telling LAPD, even the special unit that has my case, what's happening, this unit, they don't work on the weekends, which is insane.' (@ 25:46)
contacts.notes: LAPD and Secret Service later notified her when he escaped a psych facility.

contacts.what_was_asked: Arrest after she and hired security captured him.
contacts.what_institution_did: Arrested him; held on $1 million bail.
contacts.quote: We capture him. He gets arrested.
contacts.what_happened_next: Held a year on $1M bail awaiting trial.

contacts.what_was_asked: Prosecute rape and death threats; trial.
contacts.what_institution_did: Dropped the death threats, then took a plea to felony stalking on the courthouse steps.
contacts.quote: They didn't use any of my death threats, they just let them go.
contacts.what_happened_next: 'I decided to just accept the plea because I was really not given much of a choice.'

contacts.what_institution_did: Felony stalking conviction; four-year max cut to two under Prop 57.
contacts.quote: even though I got my stalker on felony stalking max, which should be a four year sentence, it was immediately turned into two. All that work for two years.
contacts.what_happened_next: Released December 2019.
contacts.notes: She calls the felony conviction 'a big win'.

contacts.institution: police / courts and Department of Corrections (post-release)
contacts.what_institution_did: Jailed him repeatedly on short misdemeanors; ankle monitor not actually monitored.
contacts.quote: I've lost track of how many times I've put him back in jail. Unfortunately, every time since it's been a misdemeanor, so it's not very long, because he's gotten slicker about how he does it.
contacts.what_happened_next: He is free in LA with no monitoring; no direct contact for almost a year.
contacts.notes: 'nobody at the Department of Corrections is monitoring that thing.' (@ 32:48)

persons.outcome_quote: As for my stalker, the convicted one, I've had to put him in jail multiple times. Unfortunately, I've only been able to get him on misdemeanors after the original felony so it's not for very long.
persons.decisive_work_quote: So I caught my own stalker. I had to do that. I didn't have a choice.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: about six years after her first police report (2011 to the 2017 arrest)
persons.notes: Stalker named on air; not used. She also mentions being a survivor of domestic violence and sexual assault at other times; no story told, so no separate records. Victim services: she did not know she was eligible and got none for a year (not a contact). Trailer for her episode at end of s19-e13.

persons.name: Peggy Klingke
persons.harm: Stalked and murdered by her ex-boyfriend; her sister later found no laws or resources that could have protected her.

quotes.quote: All the signs were there of Peggy being in danger, Peggy being stalked, leading up to her murder.

persons.outcome_quote: Peggy Klingke, who was stocked and murdered by her ex-boyfriend.

contacts.quote: That [perpetrator] received instead of jail time, a two year conditional sentence for house arrest.

contacts.notes: Perpetrator name in the quote replaced with [perpetrator].

coder_notes: All eight chunk files read in full to their stated last lines (s19_06 and s19_08 reading was interrupted by usage limits and resumed exactly where notes.md left off). Season 19 is a stalking season: Amy (e1-e5 plus WCN update), Sarah (e6-e8), two What Came Next season-14 updates (Kaelin, Melissa and their daughters), a community catch-up (host's Dallas hotel incident, Sarah and Amy updates, update on an earlier doula-fraud story), Jennifer Khalifa (e12-e13), Lenora Claire (finale), a Data Points: Racism episode (educational only, no person stories) and a trailer. Perpetrators' names appear on air and in show notes and are replaced with [perpetrator] in quotes. Wherever a quotation contained a perpetrator's name it was replaced with [perpetrator] and nothing else was changed. Season 14 and the earlier doula season were not given to me, so those update records are low confidence. Judgment calls: Amy coded protected though partly_protected is defensible; Jennifer's husband and Emerson coded protected with low confidence; Melissa's outcome is thinly supported; Peggy Klingke is borderline between a record and a bare mention. Unassigned: read INDEX and both Lenora Claire Data Points episodes in full; neither updates her story.
